extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology that includes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar for open research in computational linguistics.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi; Yanxia Qin; Benjamin Aw; Niranjana Unnithan; Min-Yen Kan
extraction.citeAs: Rohatgi, Shaurya; Qin, Yanxia; Aw, Benjamin; Unnithan, Niranjana; Kan, Min-Yen. 2023. The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The corpus was built by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology, extracting full text from PDFs, extracting figures and tables, and enriching papers with additional information from Semantic Scholar's API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Certain fields are only available for a subset of papers; for example, only 16.8% of papers have an arXiv paper ID.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF documents and metadata from the ACL Anthology, plus additional information from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: They removed PDF files longer than 50 pages, extracted full text from PDFs using GROBID, extracted figures and tables using PDFFigures, and stored figures separately from textual data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For topic classification, the authors crawled published papers from several online CL conferences between 2020 and 2022 together with their topics from conference websites, aligned them with ACL OCL, and used the resulting 2,545 documents with 21 topics as training and testing data. They also released model-predicted silver topic labels with OCL.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: They evaluated topic classification using 5-fold cross-validation and reported that model-predicted topics are silver data, with errors arising from insufficient training samples and topic overlap.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID; PDFFigures; Semantic Scholar Graph API; langdetect; BART-large-MNLI; SciBERT; SPECTER
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates by downloading and processing newly added ACL Anthology papers, and the authors plan to update OCL yearly to keep it alive.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus is intended to advance open scientific research, accelerate scientific progress, and promote reproducibility in computational linguistics.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The topic analysis is affected by bias toward dominant topics in top-cited papers, and many languages remain underrepresented in the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The corpus is limited to peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers from the ACL Anthology, is not comprehensive beyond that source, full-text quality is constrained by PDF extraction limitations, and the corpus is unlabeled for task-specific annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Open research in computational linguistics; temporal topic trend analysis; topic analyses and topic-aided tasks; document-level terminology detection; coreference resolution; pre-training scientific large language models; fine-tuning general LLMs; summarization; related work generation; information extraction from specific sections; historical language change analysis; knowledge graph construction; and multimodal research tasks.

name.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain.

description.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. Integrating and enhancing the previous versions of the ACL Anthology, the ACL OCL contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar).

isLiveDataset.evidence: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We start by crawling the PDF files and metadata from the source ACL Anthology. We then pass the PDF files through the full-text extraction process. We enhance this data using Semantic Scholar’s API to fetch additional information about OCL papers.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website. We use its Graph API8 to connect an OCL document to its corresponding document in S2AG.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: We note that certain fields are only valid on a portion of the papers. For example, only 16.8% of OCL papers have arxiv_paper_id, indicating a corresponding version in arXiv.org.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: From the ACL Anthology, we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website. We enhance this data using Semantic Scholar’s API to fetch additional information about OCL papers.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: The OCL corpus includes 73,285 papers hosted by the ACL Anthology published from 1952 to September 2022.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages, which are mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks. After an extensive comparison with open-source toolkits such as PDFBox and pdfminer.six, we use GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files. Due to the limitations of GROBID in formatting information extraction such as figures, we extract figures and tables from PDF files using PDFFigures (Clark and Diwala, 2016) following Karishma et al. (2023). The figures are stored separately from the textual data in OCL.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Topic Data Curation. We crawl published papers of several online held CL conferences (e.g., ACL 2020, EACL 2021) between 2020 and 2022, together with their topics from those websites. After aligning those papers with the data in the ACL OCL, we obtained 2545 documents classified in 21 topics in total, present in Table 4. These documents together with their topics are used as our training and testing data. Model-predicted silver topic labels are released together with OCL.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We use 5-fold cross-validation across all experiments, randomly selecting 2,036 (80%) papers balanced in each topic as our training set, and the remaining 509 (20%) as test. Note that the system-predicted topics are silver data, which we detail later. Two works in Resource & Evaluation, namely BLEU (Papineni et al., 2002) and ROUGE (Lin, 2004), are incorrectly predicted due to insufficient training samples and high overlap with other topics.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: After an extensive comparison with open-source toolkits such as PDFBox and pdfminer.six, we use GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files. Due to the limitations of GROBID in formatting information extraction such as figures, we extract figures and tables from PDF files using PDFFigures (Clark and Diwala, 2016) following Karishma et al. (2023). We use its Graph API8 to connect an OCL document to its corresponding document in S2AG. To detect the language in which a document is written, we utilize a public language detection toolkit10 (Shuyo, 2010) with its title and abstract as inputs. We follow their work and use a variant model BART-large-MNLI11 to model the topic classification task as an inference task. In addition, we consider pre-trained language models trained from scientific documents, namely SciBERT (Maheshwari et al., 2021) and SPECTER (Cohan et al., 2020).

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The dataset undergoes annual updates, during which we download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology. In the future, we will work on the data currency of OCL, which aims to keep OCL up-to-date with the ACL Anthology data. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Building scholarly corpora for open research accelerates scientific progress and promotes reproducibility in research by providing researchers with accessible and standardized data resources.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The 87% accuracy is higher than an expected 69% accuracy tested on the STop test set in Table 5, mainly because of the bias in the distribution of top-cited papers towards dominant topics (e.g., MT). Prior research (Ranathunga and de Silva, 2022) on the representation of low-resource languages in the ACL Anthology found that numerous languages remain underrepresented.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC (Lo et al., 2020), since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology. Due to constraints on budget, only open-source toolkits are considered, although it is acknowledged that some paid PDF2text services might yield higher-quality full texts. The OCL corpus is an unlabeled resource, lacking annotations for specific tasks that require labels.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. We spotlight how ACL OCL applies to observe trends in computational linguistics. OCL aids tasks that demand complete textual content from scientific papers, such as document-level terminology detection, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models like Galactica (Taylor et al., 2022) or fine-tuning a general LLM like Llama (Touvron et al., 2023).
